heard: A piece of the moon's blinding face is sitting in Madagascar. Looking up from Earth, the bright lunar highlands visible without a telescope are made of anorthosite. Over four billion years ago, lightweight minerals floated atop a lunar magma ocean to freeze into crust. Apollo astronauts hauled back tiny fragments, forcing researchers to hunt for larger rock analogs on Earth. While smaller deposits sit in Montana, Southern Madagascar holds an exposure of unprecedented scale. Astronauts aboard the space station photographed a brilliant, 40-square-mile white circle blazing against the landscape. Formed at least 600 million years ago, this massive lunar-like dome survived the collision that assembled Gondwana. No spacecraft is required to see the ancient geology that illuminates our night sky. You
